text: If \(F(x) = \left(f\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right)^2+\left(g\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\right)^2\), where \(f''(x) = -f(x)\) and \(g(x) = f'(x)\), and \(F(5) = 5\), then \(F(10)\) is equal to
solution:
\(F'(x) = 2f\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)f'\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\cdot\frac{1}{2} + 2g\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)g'\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\cdot\frac{1}{2}\).

Since \(f' = g\) and \(g' = f'' = -f\), this is \(f\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)g\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) - g\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)f\!\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) = 0\).

So \(F\) is constant and \(F(10) = F(5) = 5\). Option A.

solution:
\(\sqrt{\tan x} + \sqrt{\cot x} = \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x\cos x}}\).

Put \(t = \sin x - \cos x\), so \(dt = (\cos x + \sin x)\,dx\) and \(t^2 = 1 - 2\sin x\cos x\), giving \(\sin x\cos x = \frac{1 - t^2}{2}\).

The integral becomes \(\int \frac{\sqrt{2}\,dt}{\sqrt{1 - t^2}} = \sqrt{2}\sin^{-1}t + c = \sqrt{2}\sin^{-1}(\sin x - \cos x) + c\). Option A.
